text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi Congress of Trade Union (MCTU) Secretary General Francis Antonio said on Wednesday the government had cheated the union after it issued a directive to cut salaries for all civil servants. The directive was aimed at those who went on strike in April.

- Retired Anglican Bishop Nathaniel Aipa, whose church charged him with sexual immorality and misappropriation of funds, has been cleared by a church court which sat in Blantyre last Thursday and Friday.
- Malawian international and veteran broadcaster, Dyson Mzumara hired by German Radio Deutsche Welle, died on Wednesday in a Blantyre hospital while on vacation.

- Despite an explicit warrant, police are failing to arrest a Blantyre-based white businessman. The warrant was issued by the High Court after the businessman failed to attend court after being sued for allegedly seizing property.

- The inquest into the death of former Army General Manken Chigawa, who was gunned by down by car thieves in April, 1995, in Ntcheu, resumes today at Zomba Magistrate's court, more than 60km north east of Blantyre.
